title: Inside Courtyard's Sneaker Packs: Grails, Lore & the Sneaker Reset
summary: Nike is cutting supply, but Courtyard’s new $275 Sneaker Packs are bringing back true scarcity with authenticated grails from Off-White, Supreme, and rare PEs.
body_markdown:
In 2022, Courtyard’s very first packs debuted, featuring roughly 1,000[professionally graded](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/welcome-to-card-school-the-difference-between-slabbed-cards-and-their-raw-counterparts)[Pokémon cards](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=pkmn) . Since then, we’ve worked hard to give collectors access to grails from holo[Charizard](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Charizard&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) s and[LeBron](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=LeBron%20James&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) rookies, as we branched out from[Snorlax](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Snorlax&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) to sports. As collecting has changed over time, we’ve expanded our inventory even further; now, you can find everything from[high-end watches](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=watches) and[bronze age comics](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=watches) to[ancient coins](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=comics) on Courtyard. More recently, we launched our newest category: sneakers.


Each of our five size-specific, authenticated[Sneaker Packs](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=sneakers) cost $275 and hold one authenticated deadstock Nike or Jordan pair that collectors can ship home, hold in the Courtyard vault, sell at fair market value via an instant buyback offer, or list on the marketplace with 0% fees. Talk about options.


However, as the sneaker market continues to evolve, we wanted to not only talk about the heat inside our Sneaker Packs, but how the larger industry is changing, and how once-rare pairs are becoming more common—something that’s ignited a fiery debate within the sneakerhead community.


To quote Nasir Jones, “[Nikes on my feet keep my cypher complete](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e5PnuIRnJW8&list=RDe5PnuIRnJW8&start_radio=1) .”


## **What’s Inside Courtyard’s Sneaker Packs**


The kicks found inside our new authenticated Sneaker Packs are constantly rotating, but the heavy hitters lean heavily into recent market favorites: SB Dunks, collabs, and rarities. As of writing, the most-valuable sneaks in these packs have a fair market value of $4,400, but, as every sneakerhead knows, it’s not about the money—it’s about the story.


- [Supreme x Nike SB Dunk Low Pro "White Cement" (2002)](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/mens-9-to-9-5-sneakers-pack) **:**


- The first collaboration between streetwear legends Supreme and Nike SB brought the Air Jordan 3's elephant print to the Dunk. Only[500 pairs of each cement colorway](https://www.inputmag.com/style/supreme-nike-sb-dunk-low-blue-gold-stars-release-info) were reportedly released, through Supreme's New York and Tokyo stores.


- [Off-White x Air Jordan 1 High "Chicago" (2017)](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/mens-10-to-10-5-sneakers-pack) **:**


- Virgil Abloh's deconstructed Jordan 1 was the only Jordan in his Nike collection, "The Ten.” With "AIR" printed on the midsole and a zip tie on the collar, these felt quintessentially Abloh, and, unsurprisingly,[Highsnobiety readers voted it the best sneaker of 2017](https://www.highsnobiety.com/p/nike-off-white-guide/) . RIP to the definition of a legend.


- [Ben & Jerry's x Nike SB Dunk Low "Chunky Dunky" (2020)](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/mens-9-to-9-5-sneakers-pack) **:**


- It dropped at skate shops on May 23, 2020 for $100, with cow print, tie-dye details, and a Swoosh that looks like it's melting.[Complex called it 2020's most hyped release](https://www.complex.com/sneakers/a/mike-destefano/best-sneaker-packaging) , and some pairs came in packaging made to look like a Ben & Jerry's pint. (If you lost the raffle, you remember, and it hurts.)


- [Travis Scott x Air Jordan 4 "Cactus Jack" (2018)](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/mens-10-to-10-5-sneakers-pack) **:**


- A tribute to the Houston Oilers, these were released alongside Scott's block party in downtown Houston—which[ended early after more than 3,000 people showed up](https://abc13.com/travis-scott-hosts-block-party-ahead-of-shoe-release/3579156/) .


- [Eminem x Air Jordan 2 "The Way I Am" (2008)](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/mens-10-to-10-5-sneakers-pack) **:**


- Made to celebrate Eminem's autobiography, the 2s were limited to just[313 pairs](https://www.sneakerfreaker.com/releases/eminem-x-air-jordan-4-encore-JJ3098-400-price-buy-release-date) , a nod to Detroit's area code.


- [Nike SB Dunk "Three Bears" (2006)](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/mens-11-to-11-5-sneakers-pack) **:**


- Baby Bear Low, Mama Bear Mid, and Papa Bear High, all in faux fur. The set[reportedly sat on shelves](https://www.sneakerfreaker.com/features/the-forgotten-nike-sb-dunks-of-yesteryear) until Travis Scott himself was spotted in the Papa Bears in 2018. The packs currently list all three: Baby Bear and Papa Bear in the[11-11.5 pack](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/mens-11-to-11-5-sneakers-pack) and Mama Bear in the[9-9.5 pack](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/mens-9-to-9-5-sneakers-pack) .


- [Nike SB Air Force 1 Low "Pink Foam" Friends & Family](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/mens-9-to-9-5-sneakers-pack) **:**


- This is the newest pair on the list—and one of the only ones that never had a formal release. Nike[gave it to skate shop owners](https://www.soleretriever.com/news/articles/nike-sb-air-force-1-friends-and-family-skate-shop-owners) at an SB summit in Beaverton, Oregon this January. Can you imagine?


- [Air Jordan 1 Low OG "Michigan" PE (2023)](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/mens-10-to-10-5-sneakers-pack) **:**


- A player exclusive[Jordan Brand made for Michigan football](https://sneakernews.com/?p=1178272) . Every member of the team and staff got a pair, limiting the run to less than 300 pairs.


"Sneakerheads have always cared more about the story than the price tag," said Courtyard’s Head of Social, Jake Spinowitz. "Supreme Dunks from 2002, a Houston Oilers Jordan 4, a Detroit-area-code Jordan 2: people still talk about those pairs years later because of what they meant when they dropped. That's the type of story we want collectors to find—and share—when they open a pack."


## **Why Courtyard’s Sneaker Selection Hits Different**


For the past few years, sneakers have transcended sidewalks, as scalpers have turned what was once an everyday item into a coveted collectible that was nearly impossible to get. As you can see from the list above, it wasn’t always that way. Sneakers used to be released in skate shops, and even sit on shelves without demand. Imagine the horror!


We won’t dare follow up Nas by quoting Justin Timberlake, but, as the saying says, what goes around, comes around.


On October 1st, Nike CEO Elliott Hill said the company had been[“oversupplying our iconic retro product.”](https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_financials/2027/q1/NIKE-Inc-Q1FY27-OFFICIAL-Transcript_-FINAL.pdf) The sneaker world has been working through the fallout ever since. Dunk and Jordan retro supply is getting cut, and resale prices on plenty of recent releases sit below retail. (*fakes gasping in horror*)


That’s why we carefully curated a list of meaningful shoes that are both rare and full of lore. We’re of the opinion that everyone should be able to walk into a sneaker shop and grab a pair of Dunks—or whatever classic silhouette they favor, from Air Maxes to adidas Gazelle’s; not every shoe should be scarce, but not every shoe deserves a million pairs, either.


## **The Great Sneaker Reset**


Nike’s first-quarter revenue fell 4% to *just* $11.2 billion. Hill said Nike cut Dunk revenue by nearly 50% in the quarter, a roughly $200 million hit to Sportswear, and that Jordan Brand, which accounts for 13% of Nike’s business, saw revenues fall by a “mid-teens” percent.


To counter this, Nike is going back to basics.


The Swoosh plans to reduce the volume and frequency of specific Jordan retro launches, using the Air Jordan 1 as a template, with North America set to take the biggest near-term impact. According to Hypebeast’s review of published release data, Jordan Brand averaged about 10 retro releases *per month* from October 2025 through September 2026, including 19 in February alone. Air Jordan 1 High colorways have already dropped from 20 in 2021 to 12 in 2026, while only 13 of September’s 30 launches sold out at retail and then traded at a premium on StockX and GOAT, down from 19 a year earlier, according to[Footwear News](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/sneaker-resale-market-had-sluggish-163420876.html) . Case in point: six of the seven Jordan retros released in September traded at a discount to retail on resale platforms, and, per[a SneakerPing study covered by Baller Alert](https://balleralert.com/sneaker-resale-culture-market-decline/) , nearly 60% of the 3,538 releases since August 2024 most recently sold below retail, including more than 70% of Jordan releases.


That’s why the same scarcity that built Jordan Brand is back on the menu, which might be why the same report notes that rare collabs still command major prices, and that Jordan sales were up 6% in the first half of 2026.


## **How to Get Rare Sneakers on Courtyard**


Nike is trying to make fewer shoes in an effort to make sneakers feel special again—but many of the pairs found in[Courtyard’s Sneaker Packs](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/?category=sneakers) were rare to begin with, coming from skate shop runs, friends and family gifts, and player exclusives.


From classic staples, premium limited collabs, and grails that rarely hit the open market, these packs have stories to tell. Time to add your own by picking a size, ripping a pack, and sharing the result—or selling it to your fellow collectors on the[Courtyard Marketplace](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Nike%20SB%20Dunk&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) .
